body: Can you add a reproducer project please?

hi geoand,

sure, no problem. You can find it here: https://github.com/ferencbeutel4711/repro-18885

just run it with quarkusDev, after roughly 15 seconds you will see the exception.

For your convenience, I have also added a log output with the classname used for bean resolving - in quarkus 1.12.x, it is `TestJob`, in 1.13.x+, it is `TestJob_Subclass`

Thanks!

I don't know much about Quarkus, but I'll have a look anyway. If I can't figure it out, I'll pull in others who have actually worked in this area.

The easy workaround for now is to add: `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled=false` you `application.properties`. More information about this can be found [here](https://quarkus.io/guides/cdi-reference#quarkus-arc_quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled).
It looks like Arc should not be trying to create a proxy in this case (as there is no default constructor), but in any case that's one for @mkouba

> > I don't know much about Quarkus, but I'll have a look anyway....
> 
> @geoand sure you do :-)
> 
> Anyway, thanks for having a look at the issue.

Haha, I meant Quartz :P

Ok, so the exception comes from the `org.quartz.simpl.SimpleJobFactory` which attempts to instantiate a `TestJob_Subclass` via a no-args constructor but the subclass obviously does not declare a no-args constructor. It probably works with  `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled=false` because the original class is transformed with the `allopen` plugin (because in fact the `HouseKeepingJob` class itself does not declare a no-args constructor).

> It looks like Arc should not be trying to create a proxy in this case (as there is no default constructor), but in any case that's one for @mkouba

ArC is not trying to create a proxy but an intercepted subclass which is needed in the dev mode, because by default all beans are monitored. In most cases, we do add a no-args constructor automatically but in this particular case:
1. It's not needed because intercepted subclasses work just fine with non-private `@Inject` constructors with params (a single constructor is considered an `@Inject` constructor)
2. The extended class (`BaseJob`) does not declare a no-args constructor either so we can't do this automatically.

To sum it up: ArC itself would work just fine but the way the job is instantiated relies on the `allopen` plugin functionality which we cannot reflect because we analyze the original classes. I'd recommend to try to switch to the [quarkus-quartz extension](https://quarkus.io/guides/quartz#scheduling-jobs-programmatically) which has a specialized `JobFactory` that should handle this situation correctly.
